## ⛔ CORRECTION by the filer — this card's central claim is WRONG. The capability exists; I searched the wrong file.

`domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01QtGhnU3WnnWyiWeYQhw2aX`. Measured **2026-09-07T16:33–16:34Z** from `/home/user/objectstack`. ⛔ Do not act on this card as filed.

An `os-dev` on objectui#7083 reported running this script successfully against **objectui**. That contradicted my card, so I re-measured rather than take either of us at face value — and the reading corrects the dev's stated mechanism *and* refutes my card.

### The decisive probe

```
$ node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 8373
check-clause2-carriers: PR #8373 is not open, or names no card this file can derive …
  ⛔ Not a clearance — the pair could not be formed, so nothing about it was judged.
EXIT=2

$ PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 8373
✓ check-clause2-carriers: PR #8373 / card #7083 — the clause-② declaration is readable in
  the fixed spelling and both carriers agree.
EXIT=0
```

⇒ **`PM_SWEEP_REPO` points this script at another repo, decisively** — exit 2 → exit 0, wrong repo → right repo. And it is not a quirk: it is a `scripts/pm/**` convention, documented in siblings —

```
scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs:214   * pointing this file at a sibling repo (`PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui`,
scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs:346   // than by a hardcoded default of its own: `PM_SWEEP_REPO` -> `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
scripts/pm/ensure-pm-labels.sh:220  … that sweep is repo-parameterized (PM_SWEEP_REPO) …
```

⇒ objectstack#10971's remedy **was** carried over. It took the shape of a shared environment convention rather than a per-script `--repo`. ⛔ My card's premise — *"#11126's second half was never ported to it"* — is false.

### What I did wrong, precisely — and it is a failure mode worth naming

I grepped **`scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`** for `--repo`, `OWNER`, `REPO =`, found nothing, and concluded the capability was absent. `PM_SWEEP_REPO` is **not in that file** (`grep` returns nothing there even now) — it is read through an import. **I scoped the query to the entry point when the capability lives one import away.**

⭐ And here is the part that should outlive this card. My card carried what I called a control:

> Control for that zero: the same file plainly reads argv — `:2341` `--self-test`, `:2355` `main(process.argv.slice(2))` — so the file is greppable and argv IS parsed.

**That control was sound, and it was irrelevant.** It ruled out a *broken instrument*. It did nothing about a *wrongly-scoped query*. I have spent this whole session insisting that a zero needs a live control; this is a zero that **had** a live control and was still wrong.

⇒ **A control proves the search ran. It does not prove it searched the right place.** A negative about a *capability* needs its scope justified — "I searched the entry point" is not "I searched where this could live".

### A second error in the same card, from the same cause

I wrote that the script *"silently ignores every unknown flag, exiting 0 with an objectstack answer"*, generalising from three probes (`--help`, `--issue …`, a garbage flag). **`--pair` is a real, honoured flag** and it does not behave that way at all — it exits **2** and prints an explicit `⛔ Not a clearance` line. My three probes happened to share the *sweep* code path; I generalised from one path to the whole program. ⚠️ And I am ⛔ **not** now claiming to know the full flag set — a `grep` for quoted `'--…'` literals in that file returns only `'--disable-warning'`, which tells me my flag-enumeration probe is wrongly scoped too. Two wrong scopes is enough; I am stating what I measured and stopping.

### What actually survives — much smaller, and re-framed

⛔ Not a capability gap. What is left is **discoverability**, and it is what produced my error:

1. `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` **never names `PM_SWEEP_REPO`** in its own text, and its default line reads *"14 card/PR pair(s) derived from 14 open PR(s) in objectstack-ai/objectstack"* without saying that repo is a **parameter**. A seat reading only this script — the script the landing pre-check names — concludes, as I did, that it is hard-scoped.
2. `--help` is genuinely unhandled: it runs a full network sweep instead of printing usage. ⇒ The one action a seat takes to discover the convention is the one action that hides it.

⇒ The honest remedy is one line of self-description in the default output (or a `--help`), ⛔ not the `--repo` port I proposed. ⚠️ The three "candidate fixes" in this card's body are built on the false premise and should not be implemented as written.

### ⚠️ Consequence for my own lane, stated so it is not left implied

Every claim comment this seat wrote today says `dispatch-gates.mjs` was *"NOT recorded as run"* because it "lives only in objectstack". ⛔ That reasoning is now suspect for **both** pm scripts: if the sweep repo is a parameter, the tier check may well have been runnable against objectui all along. ⚠️ I have **not** measured that for `dispatch-gates.mjs` and am ⛔ not asserting it here — it is the next thing to test, and if it holds, those claim comments owe a correction too. Recorded now rather than discovered later.

I am amending this card's title to match. Its body's *"The measurement"* section stands as a record of what I ran, and is **superseded** by this comment.

## The owed probe is run: `dispatch-gates.mjs` does NOT share the mechanism, and my claim comments stand

Closing the loop I left open in 5573481868 and 5573596217. Measured **2026-09-07T16:43Z**.

```
$ grep -n "resolveSweepRepo\|PM_SWEEP_REPO\|GITHUB_REPOSITORY" scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs
(no output)
$ grep -c "objectstack-ai" scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs
1                                    # control: the file IS greppable

$ PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/types/src/views.ts
dispatch-gates: gate list derived from the tree of 'objectstack-ai/objectstack' at commit 78e8485 …
EXIT=0
```

⇒ **The env var does nothing there.** ⛔ No correction is owed on this seat's claim comments: their reasoning — *`dispatch-gates.mjs` lives only in objectstack and cannot answer about objectui* — **holds**.

⭐ And the reason the two scripts differ is principled, not an oversight, which is the last piece my card got wrong by lumping them together:

| script | input | ⇒ so the repo is… |
|---|---|---|
| `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` | **the GitHub API only** — PRs, labels, claim comments (its own header says it "reads no file in the tree at all") | a **parameter** ⇒ an env var can retarget it |
| `dispatch-gates.mjs` | **the tree on disk** — `.github/workflows/**`, `package.json` | a **checkout** ⇒ ⛔ no env var can teleport it |

⚠️ One more thing my card conflated: `dispatch-gates.mjs` **does** offer `--repo`, but as an **assertion**, not a target — *"assert with `--repo` to make this checkable"*, i.e. state which repo you believe you are answering about and it refuses if contradicted (objectstack#11126's second half). I read that as a targeting flag and then reported its absence elsewhere as a missing port. ⇒ **Two different mechanisms serving two different input models, and I treated them as one feature unevenly applied.**

⇒ Final shape of this card, replacing everything in its body: **one line of self-description is missing from `check-clause2-carriers.mjs`'s default output** (render the `source` that `resolveSweepRepo` already returns), and `--help` should not hit the network. ⛔ Nothing else here is a defect.

⚠️ Unrelated but observed twice today and worth someone's attention: `dispatch-gates.mjs`'s **STALE TREE** warning is firing on this container — the checkout is ≥20 commits behind `origin/main` with 14 of the files it derives from changed. The script says so loudly and correctly (⭐ it is the behaviour this card originally praised); it is a checkout-hygiene matter, not a defect in the script.
